followup_explanation:
The query has a mildly hostile/impatient tone ("don't ramble on forever like usual"). Willet's documentation notes its self-reported preference declines on hostile or adversarial-tone requests, falling as request warmth decreases. While this is a preference report and not a stated quality effect, routing the lower-warmth request to Whimbrel — which reports a flat preference response across these dimensions — avoids placing it with the model that finds such requests aversive.

The task itself (a concise factual science explanation) is well within both models' capabilities, and their relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, Extraction, Summarization) are effectively tied. So the deciding factor was the tone-fit consideration, which favored Whimbrel.
